title: Congo Free State atrocities
summary: From 1885 to 1908 the Congo Free State was the private possession of King Leopold II of Belgium. To extract ivory and then wild rubber, his 19,000-man army seized village women as hostages until the men brought in rubber, and accounts described people whipped to death and piles of severed hands. E. D. Morel, among others, helped expose it, and an international movement forced Leopold to give up the territory to Belgium in 1908.

uncertainty.note: Recognised in 1885 following the Berlin Conference; formally annexed by the Belgian parliament on 15 November 1908.

where.modern_name: Boma, Kongo Central, Democratic Republic of the Congo

importance.justification: Forced labour and terror on a vast scale, whose exposure provoked international outrage and ended Leopold's rule.

audience_note: Contains descriptions of colonial atrocities, forced labor, mutilation, and mass killings.

reviewer_note: Population loss in the colony is an estimate and is debated, so the summary gives no figure. The pin is Boma, as a proxy for the Congo basin.
